description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p20-readline.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 2 rows):
  readline.t 26 `<> does not autovivify`
  readline.t 27 `readline does not autovivify`
  -- perl-tests/readline.t:256-263 (bug #97482)

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    my $yunk = "brumbo_s473t3";
    <$yunk>;
    print "26 defined *\$yunk = ", (defined *$yunk ? 1 : 0), "\n";
    readline($yunk);
    print "27 defined *\$yunk = ", (defined *$yunk ? 1 : 0), "\n";
  perl: 26 0   27 0
  PCL : 26 1   27 1

MECHANISM: reading from a SCALAR that holds a string is a symbolic
filehandle lookup.  perl looks the glob up WITHOUT creating it (the read
fails, the symbol table is untouched); PCL's handle resolution vivifies the
glob as a side effect, so a later `defined *$name` / stash walk sees a symbol
perl never created.  Fix area: the handle-resolution path used by
`p-readline` in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md readline.t, "`<>`
autovivification (tests 26-27): `<>` and `readline` should not autovivify a
scalar when the filehandle doesn't exist."

FAMILY: autovivification side effects (#1241, #1246, #1271 are the container
and open-handle members).
subject: BUG (readline): `<$str>` and `readline($str)` AUTOVIVIFY the glob named by the string -- `defined *$yunk` is 0 in perl and 1 in PCL afterwards
